text:
tomas: heads up — after the eu-west-1 GPU scale-up last night some pods on the new nodes fail to fetch model artifacts. DNS resolves to our privatelink interface endpoint but connections get RSTs.

anika: seeing it too. quick grep of proxy logs shows bursts of TCP RST from the endpoint IP. only for pods on the new worker pool (gpu-pool-2). older nodes fine. :thinking_face:

kevin: can you paste the dig + a record? i want to confirm it isn't resolving to the wrong AZ ip.

anika: sure — result from a failing pod: 
``` 
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> tasks-control.internal.redwood
;; global options: +cmd
tasks-control.internal.redwood. 60 IN CNAME vpce-0a1b2c3d-xyz.endpoint.amazonaws.com.
vpce-0a1b2c3d-xyz.endpoint.amazonaws.com. 60 IN A 172.31.58.33
```

maria: tcpdump from the pod host while reproducing: 
```
21:02:12 IP 10.0.45.12.50014 > 172.31.58.33.443: Flags [S], seq 1234567, win 64240
21:02:12 IP 172.31.58.33.443 > 10.0.45.12.50014: Flags [R], seq 1, win 0
```

ryan: interesting — endpoint sent RST immediately. that usually means SG at endpoint rejected the connection because the source didn't match allowed sources or connection tracking state is weird. are we doing security-group referencing or CIDR allowlist on the VPC endpoint?

tomas: vpce uses sg-0f1e2d3 (custom). currently inbound 443 only from 10.0.0.0/16 (worker-subnet cidr). our new GPU workers are in same VPC but use ENI secondary IPs from a different /20 we carved out: 10.0.45.0/24. that should be covered.

kevin: could be that kube-proxy/ip-masq rules are SNATing traffic to the node's primary IP or to the NAT gateway. if the source IP the endpoint sees is the NAT GW or a different ENI, SG won't match and it RSTs. can someone check conntrack on the node?

maria: checked conntrack counters on one of the gpu nodes — conntrack table spikes when pods create many short-lived connections to endpoint. but more suspiciously the NAT gateway's active connections to 172.31.58.33 also jump during the same window. 

anika: hmm we have a short-term iptables rule that SNATs outbound to avoid hairpinning for certain CIDRs. iirc we added an exception for privatelink addresses but maybe the endpoint IP range changed after scale?

kevin: two-pronged: 1) confirm endpoint IPs are in the privatelink block and ensure iptables has a no-snat rule for them, 2) replace cidr-based SG on the endpoint with a security-group reference to the node security group (k8s-nodes-sg) so source identity survives SNAT.

anika: quick check — route table for gpu-subnet has `local` for VPC and default route to nat-0aabbccd for 0.0.0.0/0. we also have a VPC endpoint for S3 using gateway endpoints, different. interface endpoint is an ENI in the subnet with private IP 172.31.58.33. nothing odd there.

maria: i just dumped iptables nat PREROUTING from a failing node: 
```
-A POSTROUTING -s 10.0.45.0/24 -d 172.31.58.32/28 -j SNAT --to-source 10.0.10.5
```
so yep, traffic to the endpoint IP range is getting SNATed to a control-plane IP (10.0.10.5). endpoint sees source 10.0.10.5 which is not allowed by SG -> RST.

ryan: wow. that SNAT rule was added ages ago for an unrelated NAT brittle posture. proposal: remove that rule for the privatelink range and instead use sg reference on the endpoint. safer to do both: SG change + remove SNAT exception.

tomas: agree. who can make the SG change? it needs approval for cross-team infra edit.

kevin: i can patch the endpoint SG to allow the node SG as a source (security-group-id reference) — i'll create a temporary allow and then work with secops to make it permanent. i'll also add an iptables exception to the daemonset on gpu nodes to bypass SNAT for vpce cidr.

anika: note: we should be careful — if endpoint SG references node SG, we must ensure AWS allows referencing sg across AZ ENIs (it does). also if nodes are in autoscaling and use new SGs, ensure bootstrap assigns k8s-nodes-sg.

deploy-bot: [config-change] sg-0f1e2d3 inbound rule updated: allow tcp 443 from sg-0cffee11 (k8s-nodes-sg) by kevin at 2026-03-18T21:45:02Z

maria: applied iptables fix via daemonset rollout on gpu pool — removed SNAT for privatelink /28 block and added explicit rule to ACCEPT before POSTROUTING. testing now.

anika: retest from pod after fix: 
```
curl -v https://tasks-control.internal.redwood/health
* Connected to vpce-0a1b2c3d-xyz.endpoint.amazonaws.com (172.31.58.33) port 443 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

tomas: great — model pulls resumed and the deployment succeeded on gpu-pool-2. 

ryan: follow-up action items: 1) audit other privatelink endpoints for CIDR-based SGs, 2) remove legacy SNAT iptables rules or centralize them in cluster-init with clear exceptions, 3) add a monitoring alert for unexpected SNAT counts to endpoint IP ranges. i've created a ticket: INFRA-9823.

kevin: noted. i'll coordinate with secops to make the SG change permanent and document the pattern in the runbook. thanks all. :thumbsup:
